newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: SOCCER-DUTCH LOOK AT SHAPE OF THINGS TO COME.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUTCH LOOK AT SHAPE OF THINGS TO COME.

text.p: PSV Eindhoven's Philips Stadium will host an experimental soccer match next Tuesday to offer a glimpse of how the game may be ruled by high-tech in the future, according to the Dutch ANP news agency.

Technical aids will include microphones, remote cameras on the goal-lines and in the stands, computer chips and various metering equipment all of which will be monitored on a bank of screens by the side of the pitch.

The futuristic match, played between a team of veterans from the Dutch first division and a side made up from foreign players at Dutch clubs, has been organised by the Dutch professional coaches union.
The aim is to see whether technical support can help referees and improve the quality of the game.

Results from the trial match, which will not be open to press or public, will be discussed during a symposium in Brussels on December 14, ahead of the World Cup qualifier between Belgium and the Netherlands.
Former Dutch internationals Ronald Koeman and Johan Cruyff will take part in the forum, as will former international referee John Blankenstein.
A report will be forwarded to both UEFA and FIFA.
